title: MusicTwins: Training Audio-Language Models to Listen like Their Persona
abstract: arXiv:2610.32495v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: People differ in how they perceive music, what associations they make with it, what they like about it, and how they respond to it. Computational models intended to simulate people in environments that include music should account for these differences. Although LLMs have been shown to reproduce aspects of human behavior, whether audio-language models (ALMs) can reproduce a specific person's responses to textual and musical stimuli remains underexplored. We introduce MusicTwins, a framework that combines persona summaries, personal memory, and post-training to generate person-specific responses. We construct persona representations from human writings, capturing background, views, personality, writing style, and a musical profile, and post-train Audio Flamingo Next through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. translated_title: MusicTwins：训练音频-语言模型像其对应人物一样聆听音乐
translated_abstract: 人们对音乐的感知方式各不相同——他们由此产生的联想、喜欢的内容以及做出的反应都存在差异。旨在模拟音乐环境中人类的计算模型应当考虑这些差异。尽管大语言模型（LLM）已被证明能够再现人类行为的某些方面，但音频-语言模型（ALM）能否再现特定个人对文本和音乐刺激的反应仍未得到充分研究。我们提出了MusicTwins，这是一个结合人物画像摘要、个人记忆和后训练来生成针对特定个人回应的框架。我们从人类的文字中构建人物表征，捕捉其背景、观点、个性、写作风格以及音乐偏好档案，并通过监督微调和强化学习对Audio Flamingo Next进行后训练。在十个保留人物上的评估显示，Audio Flamingo Next在人物保真度方面取得了显著提升，包括……
tldr: 该论文提出MusicTwins框架，通过从人类文字中构建人物画像表征、结合个人记忆，并采用监督微调与强化学习对Audio Flamingo Next进行后训练，使音频-语言模型能够像特定个人一样对文本和音乐刺激做出个性化回应，显著提升了人物保真度。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces MusicTwins, a framework that builds persona representations from human writings and post-trains Audio Flamingo Next via supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, enabling audio-language models to respond to textual and musical stimuli like a specific individual with significantly improved persona fidelity.
